rulings.challenge_claim: The two-verse doxology cut leaves a byte-true catchword bond undisclosed: the shaming verb on which the row's closing splice ends at 17:13 recurs at 17:18, bracketing the petition that follows and arguing that 17:12-13 belongs with that petition rather than standing as its own unit; the tier-3 segmentation also groups 17:11-13, so the opening seam falls inside a single marked segment.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from bytes. The row's closing splice does end on יֵבֹ֑שׁוּ (oshb:Jer.17.13, byte tier), and 17:18 opens יֵבֹ֤שׁוּ רֹדְפַי֙ וְאַל אֵבֹ֣שָׁה אָ֔נִי (oshb:Jer.17.18, byte tier), where the same form recurs and is then negated for the speaker. The two forms differ only in cantillation: they are one string at accent_stripped tier. The count OBJECT verifies, not merely the digit: a consonantal sweep on the attested form returns (sweep: 5 verses) at MT keys - Jer.8.12, Jer.17.13, Jer.17.18, Jer.23.10, Jer.50.38 - of which exactly two stand in chapter 17, at this row's own closing verse and at the close of the 17:14-17:18 petition. Identity numbering throughout; the book's one offset zone lies in chapters 8-9 and no digit here touches it. That is a tier-1-class recurrence signal straddling this row's own closing seam, and it is absent from the row's prose: the rejected-alternative field weighs only the backward fold into 17:5-17:11, so the strongest live rival is never engaged on a two-verse span, which is the over-split direction. The segmentation observation is correctly carried as tier-3 weak single-witness corroboration (a mark at MT 17:10 and a mark at MT 17:13 leave 17:11-17:13 one segment, so the opening seam falls inside it), and absence is not treated as counterevidence. ADDED HERE, and it compounds the finding: the closing seam carries no addressee change at all. Yahweh is addressed on both sides - כָּל עֹזְבֶ֖יךָ (oshb:Jer.17.13, byte tier) is second-person singular to the vocative divine name in that same verse, and 17:14 opens רְפָאֵ֤נִי יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Jer.17.14, byte tier) with the same vocative. Only the speaker's grammatical number turns, first-person plural at מִקְדָּשֵֽׁנוּ (oshb:Jer.17.12, byte tier) to first-person singular at 17:14. The reading that a genuine speaker-focus shift carries BOTH edges therefore holds for the opening edge only. Severity medium and not higher: the opening at 17:12 does carry a byte-true turn, so the boundary is not shown to be wrong - what fails is the disclosure and the rival weighing.
rulings.remedy: WORK ORDER. (1) device_notes: add one sentence disclosing the cross-seam recurrence at this row's own closing seam - the form ending the 17:13 splice recurs at 17:18 - with the tier named (one string at accent_stripped tier; byte tier differs by cantillation) and the swept object and unit named, e.g. the attested consonantal form, (sweep: 5 verses) book-wide at MT keys, two of them in chapter 17. (2) strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the backward-only rival with the forward one - joining 17:12-13 to the 17:14-17:18 petition on that recurrence - and state why the row still stands, keeping the field to one sentence plus at most the mandated rival-disclosure sentence. TESTS the cure must pass (the tests that killed the original): the recurrence claim must carry a tier label and an adjacent digit-bearing sweep naming the swept object and its unit, with no untiered identity wording; the rejected-alternative field must engage the FORWARD join, not only the backward fold; and every mark/variant disclosure already in the row must remain correctly typed and single-witness-labelled. NOT author work: any respan folding 17:12-13 into the petition is a BOUNDARY PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption - the remedy above cures the row as spanned.

rulings.challenge_claim: The frame verification holds byte for byte, but the ketiv/qere disclosure is asymmetric - one of the two in-span notes goes unmentioned, in the very verse the rejected reading names - and the potter-word recurrence is asserted as identity without a tier and is not token-identical.
rulings.grounds: Both arms re-derived and both hold. Variant notes inside Jer.18.1-Jer.18.12 stand at MT 18:3 and MT 18:10 - two notes in the span, no third. The 18:3 note is disclosed in the row's own opening prose; the 18:10 note stands plainly in the bytes as הרעה הָרַע֙ (oshb:Jer.18.10, byte tier), and MT 18:10 is precisely the verse the rejected reading turns on, so that note is engaged without being disclosed. The omission is a SYMMETRY gap against the row's own standard, not a blanket one: the parashah layer for the same span is complete and correctly typed, PE at MT 18:4 and SAMEKH at MT 18:6, MT 18:8, MT 18:10, MT 18:12, with the PE at MT 17:27 ahead of the opening (tier-3 weak, single-witness, absence never counterevidence). The recurrence arm holds too. 18:11 carries the bare participle יוֹצֵ֤ר (oshb:Jer.18.11, byte tier) while 18:2, 18:3, 18:4 and 18:6 carry the article-bearing form הַיּוֹצֵ֑ר (oshb:Jer.18.3, byte tier). The row's sentence hedges correctly first ('reuses the same root as a verb') and then overstates, calling it the identical word rendered as the potter noun through 18:2-18:6, with no tier named on the recurrence: the tokens are not identical at byte tier; the tie holds at the consonantal level only. ADDED HERE: the consonantal tie is also not unit-bounded, which constrains what the cure may say. A sweep on the article-bearing form returns (sweep: 5 verses) at MT keys - 18:2, 18:3, 18:4, 18:6, 19:11 - while a sweep on the bare consonantal form returns (sweep: 10 verses), adding MT 10:16, 18:11, 19:1, 33:2 and 51:19, three of which carry the divine-fashioner sense rather than the craftsman. A lexeme spread that wide cannot by itself carry the internal-cohesion argument used to decline the break after 18:10. Severity low is right: the boundary is undisturbed. The onset is the prose-sermon superscription shape verse-initially with its alef-lamed linking particle at 18:1, and the internal word event at 18:5 is verse-initial - both byte-true, and neither defect touches either seam.
rulings.remedy: WORK ORDER. (1) device_notes: add the in-span ketiv/qere note at Jer.18.10 (single-witness disclosure), so both in-span notes are covered alongside the 18:3 note already carried in boundary_rationale. (2) boundary_rationale: replace the identical-word wording tied to 18:2-18:6 with a tier-named recurrence statement - the shared object is the consonantal form, not the token, since 18:11 carries the bare participle against the article-bearing form at 18:2, 18:3, 18:4 and 18:6 - and attach the digit-bearing sweep naming the swept object and unit. (3) strongest_rejected_alternative: apply the same correction, since that field repeats the same tie as its ground for declining the break after 18:10. TESTS the cure must pass: no identity/verbatim wording may stand on a recurrence without the tier named per collate truth; every recurrence digit must name the swept object (article-bearing form versus bare consonantal form) and its unit before the count; and the mark and variant disclosures for the span must be symmetric across BOTH inventories the span touches.

rulings.challenge_claim: Both stated warrants for cutting at 18:13 fail against the bytes - direct address does not stop at the claimed seam, and the cited speech formula brings no change of frame owner - while the remaining ground is translation layout, a devising-root play brackets the span on both sides undisclosed, and an in-span ketiv/qere note is not disclosed.
rulings.grounds: All five arms re-derived from bytes; each holds. (i) The seam verse opens on the back-linking particle לָכֵ֗ן (oshb:Jer.18.13, byte tier), then the messenger formula, then שַֽׁאֲלוּ נָא֙ (oshb:Jer.18.13, byte tier) - a second-person plural imperative plus the entreaty particle, the same construction already standing inside 18:11 at שׁ֣וּבוּ נָ֗א (oshb:Jer.18.11, byte tier). Direct second-person address therefore continues across the claimed seam; the third-person material the row names begins mid-verse at בְּתוּלַ֖ת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Jer.18.13, byte tier). The stated turn 'from direct second-person address to third-person description' is byte-contradicted at the row's own onset verse. (ii) The formula carries the same mouth on both sides: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.18.11, byte tier) already stands inside the command to speak to Judah, and 18:13's formula is subordinated to the verse-initial back-linking particle. Under the ruled granularity a koh-amar onset drives a row cut only WITH a frame-owner change; there is none here, so the declared speech-formula signal is not a licensed driver at this site. (iii) The poetry digit is accurate against the staged folded rendering - three, one, four, three and two opening poetry lines across 18:13-18:17 against zero across 18:1-18:12, with no continuation folds in the window - but translation line-break layout is tier-4 and is never boundary evidence in either direction, and the staged original-language material carries no verse-structure layer, so no byte fact stands behind the prose-to-poetry ground as written. (iv) The devising root brackets the row on BOTH seams and is undisclosed: וְחֹשֵׁ֥ב עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם מַֽחֲשָׁבָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.18.11, byte tier) and אַחֲרֵ֤י מַחְשְׁבוֹתֵ֨ינוּ֙ (oshb:Jer.18.12, byte tier) immediately before, וְנַחְשְׁבָ֣ה עַֽל יִרְמְיָהוּ֮ מַחֲשָׁבוֹת֒ (oshb:Jer.18.18, byte tier) immediately after. Objects verified per attested form at MT keys, not blended: the plural noun (sweep: 9 verses) book-wide, of which only MT 18:12 and MT 18:18 fall in chapters 17-19; the singular noun (sweep: 2 verses, MT 18:11 and MT 49:30); the suffixed plural (sweep: 1 verse); the cohortative verb (sweep: 1 verse). (v) The one variant note inside 18:13-18:17 stands at MT 18:16, visible in the bytes as לְשַׁמָּ֖ה שרוקת שְׁרִיק֣וֹת (oshb:Jer.18.16, byte tier), inside the charge the row's prose recites, and it is disclosed nowhere, while the parashah layer for the same span IS complete and correctly typed (SAMEKH at MT 18:12 ahead of the opening, SAMEKH at MT 18:17 at the close, tier-3 weak, single-witness). ADDED HERE, and it redirects the cure rather than rescuing the row: the very imperative that defeats the person claim is itself of the ruled discourse-imperative shape, so a candidate licensed driver is byte-present at the onset and simply unclaimed - but unlike the byte exemplars of that class at 4:5 and 10:1 it is NOT verse-initial; it stands inside the quoted divine speech the messenger formula introduces, and the same shape stands mid-verse at 18:11 without opening anything. Whether it can carry a row seam is a live question for the author wave, not settled here. Severity high: no stated ground survives byte-check, and replacing the driver re-opens the dependent fields.
rulings.remedy: WORK ORDER. (1) boundary_rationale: delete the poetry-line contrast as a boundary ground (tier-4 translation layout, barred in both directions) and correct the person statement - second-person plural address continues into the seam verse through its imperative, and the third-person description begins mid-verse at the virgin-of-Israel clause. (2) observed_substrate_signals: speech_formula.koh_amar cannot stand as the driver where the mouth is unchanged from 18:11; name instead a byte-present member of the ruled tier-1 classes and show its frame-owner or addressee change in the bytes. Because this is a driver swap, re-open the dependent fields in the same edit: observed_substrate_signals, strongest_rejected_alternative, unit_type and confidence. (3) device_notes: disclose the in-span ketiv/qere note at Jer.18.16 (single-witness), and disclose the devising-root bracket at 18:11-18:12 and 18:18 that straddles both of this row's seams, naming each attested form and its own verse count before the digit. TESTS the cure must pass (the tests that killed the original): no tier-4 layout fact may appear anywhere as a boundary ground or as counterevidence; the named driver must be byte-present at the onset AND carry the frame-owner or addressee change the ruled granularity requires, shown in the pointed bytes; the cross-seam device disclosure must name each swept form separately with its unit and digit, no blended sweep; and the span's variant-note disclosure must be symmetric with its parashah disclosure. NOT author work: folding 18:13-18:17 back into the potter unit as the divine reply to the refusal at 18:12 is a BOUNDARY PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption.

rulings.challenge_claim: The frame owner at 19:1 checks out in the bytes, but the span's stated cohesion warrant is carried by the translation - the elders thread does not exist in the Hebrew - no ketiv/qere is disclosed although a note rides on the gate name the reasoning recites, and the span is called distinct from the potter-house visit while its own opening and interpretation verses carry that unit's lexeme.
rulings.grounds: Two arms hold in full and stand as charged; the third is misframed and is corrected here; and a form-class defect neither arm names is added. ELDERS ARM UPHELD: 19:1 runs הָל֛וֹךְ וְקָנִ֥יתָ (oshb:Jer.19.1, byte tier) and then וּמִזִּקְנֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם וּמִזִּקְנֵ֖י הַכֹּהֲנִֽים (oshb:Jer.19.1, byte tier) with NO verb governing that clause - the taking is supplied on the rendering side. Every command in the span is second-person singular to the prophet, at the buying, the going out, the proclaiming, the telling, and at the breaking; the elders are never addressed in the bytes, and the witnesses at the breaking are הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֔ים הַהֹלְכִ֖ים אוֹתָֽךְ (oshb:Jer.19.10, byte tier), not elders. The prefixed elders token stands in (sweep: 1 verse) of the span, MT 19:1, and carries no governing verb there. So the closing cohesion sentence is byte-false in its third arm, while its jar arm is byte-true and is credited (sweep: 2 verses book-wide for the jar noun, MT 19:1 and MT 19:10, both inside this span). VARIANT ARM UPHELD: the span carries exactly one variant note, at MT 19:2, standing in the bytes on the gate name as שַׁ֣עַר החרסות הַֽחַרְסִ֑ית (oshb:Jer.19.2, byte tier), and no variant note is disclosed anywhere in the row, although the parashah layer for the same span IS complete and correctly typed (SAMEKH at MT 18:23 ahead of the opening, PE at MT 19:5, PE at MT 19:13, tier-3 weak, single-witness). Same symmetry failure as the mark layer's own standard in this stretch. LEXEME ARM REFINED - corrected finding: both tokens are byte-present, יוֹצֵ֣ר חָ֑רֶשׂ (oshb:Jer.19.1, byte tier) at the buying and כְּלִ֣י הַיּוֹצֵ֔ר (oshb:Jer.19.11, byte tier) at the interpretation, but this is NOT cross-seam cohesion and it does not run against the row's distinctness claim. The row's opening seam stands at 18:23 | 19:1 and the immediately preceding material carries none of the lexeme: a sweep on the bare consonantal form returns (sweep: 10 verses) at MT keys - 10:16, 18:2, 18:3, 18:4, 18:6, 18:11, 19:1, 19:11, 33:2, 51:19 - with nothing between 18:12 and 18:23, and three of those sites carry the divine-fashioner sense, so the lexeme is not unit-bounded and no byte-true device straddles this row's own seam. The distinctness the row claims rests on the sign OBJECT, the jar against the clay on the wheel, and that rests on byte-true ground. The row's own splice already carries and glosses the 19:11 token, so nothing is suppressed. What is owed is one disclosure clause, not a retraction. ADDED HERE: the onset's form-class label is byte-contested and neither arm names it. The row calls 19:1 a discourse-frame imperative and carries a matching substrate-signal key, but the bytes read הָל֛וֹךְ וְקָנִ֥יתָ (oshb:Jer.19.1, byte tier) - an infinitive absolute followed by a waw-prefixed second-person-singular suffix-conjugation form, the same commission shape standing at הָלֹ֤ךְ וְעָֽמַדְתָּ֙ (oshb:Jer.17.19, byte tier) - while the byte exemplars of that signal class at 4:5 and 10:1 are true imperatives. No morphology layer is staged, so the label is argued from the pointing plus both witnesses' renderings: the rendering reads the pair imperativally, the pointing does not carry the label. This does NOT endanger the boundary: 19:1 opens verse-initially with the divine messenger formula and the prophet as addressee, and the mouth does turn there, since the material closing at 18:23 is the prophet's own petition - so a licensed driver stands at the onset independent of the mislabelled key, and the cure is a label and key correction, not a respan. Severity medium, unchanged: the frame owner and the closing seam stand, but a stated cohesion warrant is byte-false, a disclosure is owed, and a declared signal key is mislabelled.
rulings.remedy: WORK ORDER. (1) boundary_rationale: re-cut the closing cohesion sentence - drop 'the same addressed elders', since no verb governs the elders clause at 19:1 (the taking is supplied by the rendering), the elders are never addressed, and the breaking names its witnesses differently at 19:10; keep the errand and jar arms, which are byte-true, and if the elders are retained at all state them as taken along in the rendering with the byte gap disclosed. (2) boundary_rationale and observed_substrate_signals: correct the onset's form class - 19:1 is an infinitive absolute plus a waw-prefixed second-person-singular suffix-conjugation form, not an imperative - and drop or replace the speech_formula.discourse_imperative key accordingly; if that key goes, re-open the dependent fields (strongest_rejected_alternative, unit_type, confidence) per the driver-swap rule. (3) device_notes: disclose the in-span ketiv/qere note at Jer.19.2 (single-witness), so the variant layer is symmetric with the parashah layer already disclosed. (4) device_notes: add one clause noting the potter lexeme at 19:1 and 19:11 as texture, stated correctly - a lexeme link with its tier and swept object named, NOT a cross-seam device and NOT counterevidence to the sign-object distinction. TESTS the cure must pass: every cohesion claim must survive deletion of the translation's supplied words and be re-checkable against the pointed bytes alone; every form-class label must be argued from the pointing plus both witnesses' renderings, with no morphology layer assumed; the span's variant-note disclosure must be symmetric with its mark disclosure; and any lexeme claim must name its tier, its swept form and its unit before the digit.
